SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Kamakhya Temple
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: Among the oldest of the 51 Shakti pithas, Kamakhya atop Nilachal Hill is the heart of Tantric Shakti worship, drawing pilgrims through the Ambubachi Mela each June.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Kamakhya Temple on Nilachal Hill, Guwahati
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikimedia Commons · Kamrup Metropolitan district portal

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Umananda Temple
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: The world's smallest inhabited river island, reached by ferry, holds a Shiva temple built by the Ahom king Gadadhar Singha in 1694, and is home to the rare golden langur.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Umananda Shiva temple on Peacock Island in the Brahmaputra, Guwahati
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikimedia Commons · Kamrup Metropolitan district portal

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Sivadol
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: By the great tank of the old Ahom capital stand three domed temples — Sivadol, Vishnudol and Devidol — consecrated under queen Phuleswari in 1734, with Sivadol the tallest Shiva temple in Assam.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Sivadol, the tall Shiva temple beside the Sivasagar tank

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Negheriting Shiva Doul
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: On a hillock in Golaghat district, the Ahom king Rajeswar Singha raised this brick Shiva temple in 1765 over an older stone shrine named in the Buranjis. It is a protected monument laid out on the panchayatana plan.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Negheriting Shiva Doul, the brick Shiva temple at Dergaon, Golaghat
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikipedia (citing E. A. Gait, A History of Assam) · Wikimedia Commons

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Hayagriva Madhava, Hajo
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: On one hill at Hajo, a Vishnu temple, a Muslim shrine of Pir Giyasuddin Auliya and a Buddhist stupa stand together — a living symbol of Assam's shared sanctity.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Hayagriva Madhava Temple on the hill at Hajo, Kamrup

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Sri Surya Pahar
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: A hill south-east of Goalpara where rock-cut Shiva lingas, votive stupas and deities of the Hindu, Buddhist and Jain pantheons lie scattered over about a kilometre. The Archaeological Survey of India excavated the site between 1992 and 2001 and keeps a museum here.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Sri Surya Mandir at Sri Surya Pahar, Goalpara
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Archaeological Survey of India, 2015 site report · Goalpara district portal

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Poa Mecca
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: On Garurachal Hill above Hajo stands Poa Mecca, Assam's best-known Muslim pilgrimage spot, noted as the tomb of the Sufi Pir Giyasuddin Auliya.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Poa Mecca on Garurachal Hill, Hajo

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Ajan Pir Dargah
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: On the bank of the Brahmaputra near Sivasagar town lies the dargah of Azan Fakir, the seventeenth-century Sufi poet and preacher who settled in Assam. His zikir and zari devotional songs are still sung in the valley.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Hazarat Ajan Pir Dargah at Saraguri Chapari, Sivasagar
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikipedia (Azan Fakir, citing Sahitya Akademi) · Sivasagar district portal

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Panbari Mosque
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: A three-domed mosque of the fifteenth to sixteenth century on the highway east of Dhubri town, considered the oldest mosque in Assam and an example of Bengal Sultanate architecture.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: The Panbari Mosque in Dhubri district, Assam
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikipedia (Panbari Mosque) · Archaeological Survey of India monument N-AS-3

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: On the right bank of the Brahmaputra at Dhubri, this gurdwara was established during the seventeenth-century travels of the ninth Sikh Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, who reached Dhubri in late 1669. It preserves a historical Guru Granth Sahib manuscript.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib, Dhubri
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikipedia, Gurdwara Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib (citing The Encyclopedia of Sikhism) · Wikimedia Commons

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Guwahati Baptist Church
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: Guwahati's Baptist congregation was established in 1845, in the years when the first Welsh missionaries reached the Assam valley, and it still stands in the old town near the river.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikimedia Commons (file description records the 1845 founding)

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Namphake Buddhist Monastery
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: A Tai Phake Buddhist monastery and meditation centre in a village of Dibrugarh district, with a pagoda, a golden Buddha image in the main temple and the Mucalinda Tank inside the compound.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Namphake Buddhist Temple in Namphake village, Dibrugarh district
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Dibrugarh district administration portal · Wikimedia Commons

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Tipam Phake Buddhist Monastery
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: The Tai Phake village of Tipam Fakial was established in 1835 and its Buddhist monastery in 1850, on the Burhi Dihing river. The community keeps its own language, script and ritual calendar.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Entrance of the Tipam Phake Buddhist Monastery, Dibrugarh district
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Dibrugarh district administration portal · Wikimedia Commons

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: The Sattras of Majuli
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: Majuli's monastic sattras — Auniati, Dakhinpat, Samaguri — are the living homes of Sattriya dance, mask-making and the Borgeet tradition founded by Srimanta Sankardev.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: The Doriya river channel beside the sattras of Majuli

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Auniati Satra
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: One of the oldest sattras on Majuli, Auniati belongs to the Brahma Sanghati branch of Assam's Ekasarana tradition and keeps a manuscript library with its own khol and taal instruments.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: The main entrance to the Auniati Satra, Majuli, Assam

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Barpeta Satra
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: Founded by the Vaishnavite saint Madhabdev in 1583 and first called Barpeta Than, this sattra's Kirtan Ghar is a centre of neo-Vaishnavite culture and holds manuscripts of Sankardev and Madhabdev in its math.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Barpeta Satra and its Kirtan Ghar, Barpeta
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Wikipedia, Barpeta Satra · Barpeta district portal

SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.name: Bordowa Than
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.about: The birthplace of Srimanta Sankardev and the first Namghar he built, Bordowa Than in Nagaon district is a pilgrimage site of Assam's Vaishnavas, with its Kirtan Ghar, Manikut and a small museum of the Than's own records.
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.alt: Bordowa Than at Batadrava, Nagaon district
SPIRITUAL_DESTINATIONS.source: Nagaon district administration portal · Wikipedia, Bordowa Than
